observed.quote: The following chart shows the total number of transactions processed by DOJ between 1972 and 2018.
observed.note: The official series is a denial count only. It publishes no delay count, no undetermined count, no delivery-time distribution, and it stops at 2018.

known_gaps: Why a given record produces Delay vs. Denial vs. eventual Undetermined: the notice taxonomy and the 10/30-day clocks are fully published, but no DOJ document collected describes the matching or scoring logic behind "DOJ examines its own records" (Pen. Code §28220(a)).

How often each branch fires. No official delay rate, undetermined rate, or undetermined-release rate exists in any document held; the only official time series (D8) counts denials and ends at 2018, so there is no published figure at all for 2019–2026, the exact period in which the delay/undetermined pathway became the dominant user complaint.

What the dealer's clock is after an Undetermined Notice. The DES guide states delivery is at the dealer's discretion but does not say how long that discretion lasts; a self-identified FFL reddit account describes "another 30 days to Deliver or Cancel," which is not stated in any DOJ document collected here.

Dealer-level policy variance, which is where nearly all real applicant-visible variation lives: whether a dealer releases on Undetermined at all, internal pickup cutoffs shorter than the statutory 30-day window, PPT intake-hour policies that shift the clock start, restocking fees. No DOJ document acknowledges that dealers differ on any of this.

The current total cash cost. The fee schedule held (D6) is dated 01/2020 and totals $37.19; it predates the CFET excise tax layered on firearm sales, so the fee amounts in this model are the DOJ-fee component only, not the counter price.
Whether DOJ ever revisits an Undetermined release after the firearm has been delivered — not addressed in any document collected.
The FSC exemption path is documented in fine grain (19 exemption codes), but nothing states how often exemptions are claimed or how often counter staff mis-apply them.

Practice compliance with the safe handling demonstration. The 6–12-step protocol is specified per firearm type, but no DOJ document, audit, or statistic addresses whether it is actually performed as written at the counter.
notes: This is a single statewide implementer (DOJ Bureau of Firearms) operationalized through ~2,000+ licensed dealers, so the dealer is modelled as its own actor lane: the dealer is the entire front office, and two of the process's most consequential decisions — release on Undetermined (A20) and whether to correct or cancel a bad DROS (A23/A24) — are legally the dealer's, not DOJ's. Visibility calls: the 10-day wait, the DOJ background check, the safe handling demonstration, the FSC test and its fees are all stated in applicant-facing documents held in raw/ (D5 California Firearms Laws Summary, D9 FSC Study Guide), so they are marked applicant_facing even though their operational detail comes from the dealer manuals. The Delay, Undetermined, DMV Reject and 30-Day Reject notice taxonomy does NOT appear in D5 or D9 — it exists only in the dealer-facing DES guide (D1) — which is why A08 (the urgent-notice gate) and A20 (Undetermined discretion) are staff_only despite being technically public documents; this slug is the corpus's clearest case of a back-office fact that is published but socially invisible. Ammunition eligibility checks run through the same DES screens and the same counter but are a legally distinct Prop. 63 process; only the one delivery-time coupling (A29) is modelled here, and CCW permitting, NICS/UPIN appeals and FFL03/COE collector status are treated as sibling processes, not part of this model.
